info.title: Alima API v1
info.description:
The Alima API. One version, in the path, and everything below holds across all of it.

**Authentication.** A Sanctum personal access token as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
`POST /auth/token` exchanges email + password for one (hard-throttled). A first-party
browser session is also accepted, which is how the web app's own screens reach these
endpoints.

**Token scopes.** Every endpoint but identity and a token's own lifecycle requires an
ability — `leads:read`, `outreach:write`, and so on, one read/write pair per resource
group. A token without the ability gets `403` with code `insufficient_token_ability` and
the abilities it needed in `error.details.required_abilities`. A token issued with `*` can
do everything.

**Tenancy.** Every response is scoped to the caller's current team. `POST /teams/{team}/switch`
changes it. Nothing is addressable across teams: a record belonging to another team answers
`404`, never `403`, because the existence of the record is itself not yours to know.

**Errors.** Every failure — validation, authorisation, a missing record, a throttle, an
unhandled fault — answers with the same envelope: `{"error": {"code", "message", "details"?}}`.
`code` is the contract and is safe to branch on. `message` is prose for a person and may be
translated or reworded. `details` appears only when there is something structured to say:
field errors keyed by input name on a `422`, `required_abilities` on a scope failure.

**Pagination.** List endpoints that can grow return `data`, `links` and `meta`; `per_page`
is accepted up to 100. The handful of bounded lists (a member's teams, their tokens and
devices, a team's pipeline stages and ICPs) return `data` alone.

**Versioning.** Responses carry `X-Api-Version`. The version changes only for a change that
would break a client already in the field: a field removed or renamed, a parameter narrowed,
a status code changed. Everything additive — a new endpoint, a new field, a new enum case, a
new optional filter — ships inside the current version, so last season's mobile build keeps
working. That holds only if clients tolerate fields they do not recognise, which is the one
thing asked in return. A client may pin itself by sending `X-Api-Version`; a mismatch is a
`400` rather than a best-effort answer from the wrong contract.

**Rate limits.** 60 requests a minute per token (per IP before sign-in), and a few
endpoints that spend money — drafting, sending, re-scoring, running a signal watch — carry
tighter limits of their own. A `429` carries `Retry-After`.

**Money and time.** Money is integer minor units with its currency. Timestamps are UTC
ISO-8601; a team's own clock is in its `timezone`.

post.description:
Two-factor accounts are answered in one request rather than Fortify's session-backed dance
(Phase 18): a client posts the credentials, gets a `423 auth.two_factor_required` naming
what it may send, and posts the lot again with `code` or `recovery_code`. See
{@see TwoFactorChallenge} for why that is the safe shape for a caller with no session, and
{@see ExchangeCredentialsForTokenAction} for why the challenge and the mint share one
transaction.
post.summary:
Exchange email + password — and a second factor, where the account has one — for a personal
access token (guest, throttled)

423.description: The password was right and the account has two-factor authentication on, so it is not enough on its own. `error.code` is `auth.two_factor_required` and `error.details.methods` lists what to send next (`code`, `recovery_code`). Re-post the same credentials with one of them.

code.description: Stable, machine-readable. Framework-level codes are one of `bad_request`, `unauthenticated`, `forbidden`, `insufficient_token_ability`, `not_found`, `method_not_allowed`, `gone`, `conflict`, `payload_too_large`, `unsupported_media_type`, `validation_failed`, `locked`, `too_many_requests`, `unsupported_api_version`, `server_error`, `service_unavailable`; a module raises its own, e.g. `outreach.suppressed`. Branch on this, never on the message.

message.description: Prose for a person. Translated, and free to change inside a version.

details.description: Present only when there is something structured to say — field errors keyed by input name on a 422, `required_abilities` on a token scope failure.

findings.description: The AI findings are only present once the run is ready.

pricing.description: Amounts are integer minor units; `currency` is the ISO 4217 code.

CompleteLeadTaskRequest.description:
Validates ticking a task off — or putting it back. `done` is explicit rather than a toggle, so a
retried request lands on the same state instead of flipping it back.
CompleteLeadTaskRequest.title: CompleteLeadTaskRequest

contact.description:
The person approached, when one was named. Title and name only — the address is not
part of the history of an approach, and the contact panel has it already.

ConvertSignalRequest.description:
Validates a conversion. The rules come from {@see ConvertSignalData::rules()} so the web form
(S5) and the API (S6) accept exactly the same thing, with one addition that can only be checked
here: `pipeline_stage_id` is scoped to the member's own team, so a tampered form can't file a
lead in another team's column. Authorisation lives in the controller via `SignalPolicy`.

`company_name` is **required** — the one rule the whole screen hangs off. A relocation signal
often names a person and no company, and a lead in this product is a company, so the form asks
for the person's business or holding entity rather than inventing one.
ConvertSignalRequest.title: ConvertSignalRequest

CriterionType.description: The dimensions an ICP criterion can describe. The first group are positive, **weighted** signals that raise a lead's fit score (consumed by the deterministic scorer in Scoring & Matching); the final {@see self::Exclusion} is a hard disqualifier (unweighted) — competitors, existing customers, blocked domains and the like. Values are stable storage keys; {@see self::label()} is the display name. No magic strings elsewhere.
CriterionType.title: CriterionType

leads.description:
The leads this run produced, when the relation is loaded (detail screen only). Resolved to a plain list rather than handed over as a resource collection. A nested
collection keeps its own `data` wrapper when the parent is `->resolve()`d — which the
Inertia controller does — so this arrived as `run.leads = { data: [...] }`, and the
screen, which reads `run.leads.length`, showed "No companies matched" for every run
that had actually found something.

DismissSignalRequest.description:
Validates a dismissal. The reason is **optional** — a member who just wants the card gone
shouldn't have to justify it — but must be one of the known reasons when given, so the stored
values stay usable for tuning. Authorisation lives in the controller via `SignalPolicy`.
DismissSignalRequest.title: DismissSignalRequest

DraftMessageRequest.description:
Validates a drafting request.

The two existence rules are the tenancy ones, and both are scoped to the caller's own team: a
contact id from another team's lead, or another team's brief, must fail validation rather than be
quietly ignored. Whether the *channel* may be used is not asked here — that is
{@see OutreachGuard}'s decision, and a compliance rule expressed
as a validation message would be a compliance rule a client could read off the form.
DraftMessageRequest.title: DraftMessageRequest

EnrichmentStatus.description: Where a {@see Lead} is in the enrichment pipeline (Phase 8). A lead is {@see self::Pending} when Lead Sourcing creates it, {@see self::Enriching} while the job works it, and settles {@see self::Enriched} or {@see self::Failed}. Kept separate from {@see LeadStatus} so sourcing/scoring stage and data-quality state are tracked independently. Values are stable storage keys; {@see self::label()} is the display name. No magic strings.
EnrichmentStatus.title: EnrichmentStatus

FeedbackRating.description: A member's verdict on a {@see ScoreFeedback} row: was this grade right or wrong? Deliberately binary for the MVP — it is a training signal for weight/prompt tuning, not a rating scale. Values are stable storage keys; {@see self::label()} is the display name.
FeedbackRating.title: FeedbackRating

enum: Companies you picked up and haven’t touched since.
Your best-fit companies that nobody has approached yet.
Alima’s read of the last week’s numbers.

deletes_in_days.description:
What the retention sweep will do to this row, and when — read from the same
`InsightRetention` the sweep itself uses, so the promise on screen and the rule that
deletes the row are one rule rather than two copies of it.

IssueApiTokenRequest.description: Guest request: exchange credentials for a Sanctum personal access token (mobile sign-in).

abilities.description:
Checked against the catalogue, not merely "a string": an ability nothing enforces
is a scope that reads as a restriction and isn't one (Phase 17). `min:1` matters more than it looks. An **absent** key means "no scope asked for" and
issues a full-access token, which is the right default; an **empty array** is a
caller that meant to limit the token and named nothing, and silently handing that
request full access would be the opposite of what it asked for. So the two are told
apart here rather than collapsed.

code.description:
The second factor, when the account has one (Phase 18). Both are optional here
because a client cannot know whether this account needs one until it has asked: a
first post without either gets a 423 naming what to send next, and whether what
came back is enough is the TwoFactorChallenge service's answer, not a rule's.
Constraining `code` to six digits would also refuse a recovery code typed into the
wrong box with the wrong sentence.

IssueApiTokenRequest.title: IssueApiTokenRequest

outreach_restriction.description:
A legal limit on how this company may be approached, when one applies (ADR 0007) —
e.g. a lead converted from a UAE signal, where PDPL needs prior consent that a news
article plainly isn't. Sent on every lead, not just the detail screen: Outreach
(Phase 11) and the mobile app both have to honour it, and a flag the client has to
ask for separately is a flag that gets missed.

enum: Approach via LinkedIn or a referral — not cold email.

contacts.description:
Resolved to a plain list rather than handed over as a resource collection: a nested
collection keeps its own `data` wrapper, which would leave the client reading
`lead.contacts.data` on one screen and `lead.contacts` on the next.

contacts_count.description:
The count alone for a list row (Phase 10), so the leads table can say "3 contacts"
without loading three contacts per lead.

stage.description:
--- Leads Workspace (Phase 10b), each only when the caller loaded it ---
`stage` is null when the lead has never been placed, which the board reads as "in the
 default column" (see the `pipeline_stage_id` migration) rather than as "nowhere".

score.description:
The grade against the team's active ICP (Phase 9), when `activeScore` was loaded —
enough for a badge in a list; the score screen serialises the full LeadScoreResource.

enum: Matches the profile closely — worth contacting first.
Matches part of the profile — check it before reaching out.
Little or no match with the profile.

my_feedback.description: The viewer's own verdict, when the relation was loaded scoped to them.

LeadSort.description: The orderings the leads list offers (Phase 10). Each case maps to a sortable column — or, for {@see self::Fit}, to a correlated sub-query over the lead's score against the active ICP — so a request can never name an arbitrary column. No magic strings.
LeadSort.title: LeadSort

LeadSource.description:
The external providers a lead can be discovered from, behind the {@see LeadSourceProvider} contract (ADR 0008). All three ship in the MVP: Companies House (Phase 7), Google Places and web search (Phase 7b, the latter backed by Serper — ADR 0010). Values are stable storage keys; {@see self::label()} is the display name. No magic strings. | | |---| | `companies_house`
| | `google_places`
| | `web_search`
| | `import`
Not a provider: a lead the team brought in themselves (Phase 10b CSV import). | | `manual`
Not a provider: one company a member typed in themselves — met at an event, say (Phase 10c). | | `signal`
Not a provider: a lead converted from a wealth/liquidity event in the Signals feed (ADR 0011, S4). |
LeadSource.title: LeadSource

LogContactAttemptRequest.description:
Validates a logged approach.

`occurred_at` may be in the past — a member logs yesterday's call today — but not in the future:
a contact attempt is a thing that happened, and a dated-ahead one would sit in the history as
something the team believes they have already done.
LogContactAttemptRequest.title: LogContactAttemptRequest

MoveLeadStageRequest.description:
Validates a drag between board columns. Authorisation lives in the controller via
{@see LeadPolicy::work()}; the stage's existence check is scoped to the caller's team, so you
can't move your lead into another team's column.
MoveLeadStageRequest.title: MoveLeadStageRequest

variants.description: Every variant the model offered, so switching between them costs nothing.

is_spent.description:
Whether this draft is still usable. Computed here rather than inferred from the
status on the client, so a new status can't accidentally become re-sendable.

enum: Asked us to erase their data

RecordOutcomeRequest.description:
Validates a change to a logged attempt's outcome — the common case, since the answer arrives days
after the approach.
RecordOutcomeRequest.title: RecordOutcomeRequest

RecordScoreFeedbackRequest.description:
Validates a verdict on a lead score: the rating, plus an optional short note. Authorisation is
handled in the controller via {@see LeadScorePolicy}.
RecordScoreFeedbackRequest.title: RecordScoreFeedbackRequest

RegisterPushDeviceRequest.description:
Validates a device registration.

The token's length bound is generous on purpose: FCM registration tokens are long and their
format is the provider's business, not ours. A bound exists only so a client cannot fill the
column — the only real test of a token is whether FCM accepts it, and the channel deletes the
ones it rejects.
RegisterPushDeviceRequest.title: RegisterPushDeviceRequest

ReportRange.description:
The windows the dashboard's date filter offers (Phase 13). Presets before a custom range, in the order a reader reaches for them (the `dataviz` guidance): the rolling windows first, then the calendar ones, then everything, then a date pair. A preset is only a *name* for a window — {@see ReportRange::resolve()} turns it into a {@see DateRange} in the **team's** timezone, so a Dubai team's "this month" opens on the 1st in Dubai rather than on the server. Values are stable storage keys (they go in a URL and an audit entry); {@see self::label()} is a translation key. | | |---| | `last_7_days`
| | `last_30_days`
| | `last_90_days`
| | `this_month`
| | `last_month`
| | `this_quarter`
| | `this_year`
| | `all_time`
No lower bound: every figure counts the team's whole history. The default. | | `custom`
A date pair the member typed. Falls back to {@see self::AllTime} when either is missing. |
ReportRange.title: ReportRange

SaveIcpRequest.description:
Validates an ICP create/update payload (name, flag and the full criteria set). Authorisation is
handled in the controller via {@see IcpPolicy}. Weight is only meaningful
for positive signals — it's optional here and normalised in {@see IcpData}.
SaveIcpRequest.title: SaveIcpRequest

SaveLeadNoteRequest.description:
Validates a note. Long enough for a real account of a call, short enough that the field can't be
used as a document store.
SaveLeadNoteRequest.title: SaveLeadNoteRequest

SaveLeadTaskRequest.description:
Validates a task. The assignee has to be a member of the caller's **own** team, which the
existence check scopes through the `team_user` pivot — otherwise a task could be pinned on
someone outside the team entirely.

remind_at.description:
A reminder with no due date is still a reminder ("chase this on Friday"), so the two
are validated independently rather than one requiring the other.

SaveLeadTaskRequest.title: SaveLeadTaskRequest

SaveOutreachTemplateRequest.description:
Validates a message brief.

The name is unique **per team**, and the rule is scoped that way explicitly: without the
`team_id` clause, one team naming a brief "First touch" would stop every other team from doing
the same.

subject.description:
Allowed for any channel and dropped for the ones with no subject line (see
OutreachTemplateData) — the form keeps the field mounted while the member switches
channel, and rejecting it would lose what they had typed.

SaveOutreachTemplateRequest.title: SaveOutreachTemplateRequest

SaveSignalWatchRequest.description:
Validates a watch on create and update. The rules come from {@see SignalWatchData::rules()} so
the web (S5) and API (S6) endpoints can't drift apart on what a watch may be, with the ICP's
existence scoped to the member's own team here — the one check that needs the request to know
who is asking. Authorisation lives in the controller via `SignalWatchPolicy`.

`market` is deliberately **not** accepted: v1 is UAE-only and the value is set by the DTO (see
{@see SignalWatchData::DEFAULT_MARKET}), so a posted market is ignored rather than honoured into
a watch that would silently find nothing.
SaveSignalWatchRequest.title: SaveSignalWatchRequest

ScoreGrade.description: The A–D grade of a {@see LeadScore}: a coarse, sortable bucket over the hybrid 0–100 fit score so a member can scan a list without reading numbers. Thresholds come from `config/scoring.php` (not hard-coded) so a team's expectations can be tuned without a migration. Values are stable storage keys; {@see self::label()} is the display name. No magic strings.
ScoreGrade.title: ScoreGrade

SetLeadAssigneesRequest.description:
Validates who is working a lead — the whole set, so the screen sends what it wants and the Action
works out the difference. Each id has to be a member of the caller's own team.
SetLeadAssigneesRequest.title: SetLeadAssigneesRequest

enum: A company is sold or a founder exits — a classic liquidity event.
A business raises a funding round, putting fresh capital in founders’ hands.
A founder, executive or family office relocates to the market.

amount_minor.description:
Integer minor units + an ISO code, formatted on the client in the team's locale
(CLAUDE.md money rule) — never a pre-formatted string.

deletes_in_days.description:
What the retention sweep will do to this row, and when (S6 / compliance.md §5a).
Sent rather than computed on the client, and read from the same `SignalRetention`
the sweep itself uses — so the promise on screen and the rule that deletes the row
are the same rule, not two copies of it.

watch.description: The watch that found it, when loaded — so a team running several knows which.

lead.description:
Where a converted signal went. Null on an unconverted one, and null on a converted
one whose lead has since been deleted (the FK nulls), which the card reads as "the
 lead is gone" rather than "never converted".

ignore_domains.description: The team's own exclusion list (S6) — their competitors, which only they can know.

next_due_at.description:
When the hourly scheduler will next consider it. Null for a watch that has never run
(it is due now) or one that is paused (it isn't due at all).

runs.description:
Resolved to a plain list rather than handed over as a resource collection: a nested
collection keeps its own `data` wrapper, which would leave the client reading
`watch.runs.data` here and `watch.runs` elsewhere.

StartDiscoveryRequest.description:
Validates a "start discovery" payload. Authorisation lives in the controller via
{@see DiscoveryRunPolicy}. `sources` is one or more live providers (the run fans out to one
{@see DiscoveryRun} per source); `icp_id`, if given, is checked to
belong to the team. `limit` is bounded by config.
StartDiscoveryRequest.title: StartDiscoveryRequest

StoreLeadRequest.description:
Validates a hand-added lead. The rules come from {@see CreateLeadData::rules()} so the web form
and `/api/v1` accept exactly the same thing, with one addition that can only be checked here:
`pipeline_stage_id` is scoped to the member's own team, so a tampered form can't file a lead in
another team's column. Authorisation lives in the controller via `LeadPolicy::create`.

`company_name` is the only required field — see {@see CreateLeadData} for why the rest are not.

country.description:
Two letters or nothing: the column is char(2), so "United Kingdom" would otherwise be
stored as "UN".

StoreLeadRequest.title: StoreLeadRequest

SuppressIdentityRequest.description:
Validates an entry a team is adding to its own do-not-contact list.

Note what the rules do *not* include: a `scope`. A member cannot choose to write a global entry —
that scope belongs to the platform acting on a person's own words (see
{@see SuppressIdentityAction}), and offering it as a field would
mean validating a request that must never be honoured.

The value's shape is checked by the type's own normaliser rather than here: `email` would reject
a pasted URL for a domain entry, and `regex` can't express "digits, however they are spaced".
An unusable value comes back as a domain exception the member can read.
SuppressIdentityRequest.title: SuppressIdentityRequest

SyncLeadTagsRequest.description:
Validates a lead's whole tag set, by name. Names rather than ids, because a tag is created on
first use — asking the client to create the tag and then attach it would be two round trips and
a chance to leave an orphan behind.
SyncLeadTagsRequest.title: SyncLeadTagsRequest

UpdateMessageRequest.description:
Validates an edit to a draft's text — the member rewriting what the model wrote, which is the
expected workflow rather than an exception to it.

Only the words are editable. Channel, tone, locale and the chosen contact are not: changing any
of them changes what the guard has already decided about, and a member who wants a different
channel is asking for a different draft.
UpdateMessageRequest.title: UpdateMessageRequest

errors.description: A detailed description of each field that failed validation.
